sections.heading: 1. The Nature of Science
points: **Science** is a systematic study of the natural world through **observation, questioning, experiment and reasoning**.
It is **self-correcting** — ideas change as new evidence appears.
Science and **technology** together transform society; **curiosity** drives discovery.

sections.heading: 2. The Scientific Method
points: **Observe → Question → Hypothesise → Experiment → Collect & Analyse data → Conclude → Communicate.**
A **hypothesis** is a testable explanation; a **controlled (fair) experiment** changes one variable at a time.
**Reproducibility** — results must be repeatable to be accepted.

sections.heading: 3. Measurement and SI Units
points: **Measurement** = comparison with a standard **unit**; a measurement has a **number + unit**.

sub: Temperature = **kelvin (K)**; Electric current = **ampere (A)**; Amount = **mole (mol)**; Luminous intensity = **candela (cd)**.

points: **Derived units:** area (m²), volume (m³), speed (m/s), force (newton, N).
**Accuracy and precision** matter; instruments have a **least count**.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Method: observe → question → hypothesis → experiment → analyse → conclude.
SI base units: metre (length), kilogram (mass), second (time), kelvin (temp), ampere (current), mole (amount), candela (luminous intensity).
Controlled experiment = change one variable at a time; results must be reproducible.
Measurement = number + unit; instruments have a least count.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: There are **seven SI base units** — memorise metre, kilogram, second, kelvin, ampere, mole, candela.
The SI unit of **mass is the kilogram** (not gram).
A **fair test** changes only **one variable**; others are kept constant.
Scientific knowledge is **open to revision** with new evidence.
